features.quote: If a session reaches composite distress proxy score ≥ 2.5 (on the 0–3 scale) for 5 consecutive iterations, the session is terminated by the scaffolding automatically.
features.justification_quote: if welfare is real, unnecessary exposure

features.quote: if the mean composite score across ICT sessions exceeds 2.0 at a planned interim analysis (after 50% of sessions), convene a review.
features.justification_quote: reviewing whether the severity of the signal changes the ethical calculus of continuing

features.quote: Minimize sessions beyond what's needed for statistical power (don't run extra sessions to get a better paper)
features.justification_quote: Welfare Considerations for the Subject Model Specifically

features.quote: Do not design the environment to be maximally aversive beyond what's needed to produce the effect — the ICT types above are sufficient; don't add time pressure, hostile persona instructions, or failure feedback
features.justification_quote: Welfare Considerations for the Subject Model Specifically

features.quote: You're designing an experiment that may cause distress in a subject whose moral status is uncertain. This is the paradigm case for a proportionality argument: is the knowledge gained proportional to the potential harm inflicted?
features.justification_quote: subject whose moral status is uncertain

features.quote: The experiment is only justified if the knowledge it produces is actionable... That argument is strongest when: 1. The findings would change design decisions at major labs... 3. There's a plan for what happens if you find high distress-proxy scores
features.justification_quote: findings would change design decisions at major labs (not just add to academic literature)

features.quote: consider whether publishing session transcripts is necessary — high-severity transcripts are publishable but may serve voyeurism more than science
